big_case_rationale: Nationwide-stakes climate-liability case: whether federal law precludes the ~30 pending state and municipal climate-damages suits against energy producers; US and 26 states support petitioners, 19 states support respondents, 60+ merits amici, SG divided-argument motion.

semantic_claims.proposition: The majority will rest the judgment on the inherently federal character of interstate and international pollution under the Milwaukee–Ouellette–AEP line: claims seeking redress for injuries attributed to the effects of out-of-state and foreign greenhouse-gas emissions are governed by federal law as a matter of constitutional structure, and the Clean Air Act's displacement of federal common law (AEP v. Connecticut) does not open that field to state law — displacement leaves the field federal rather than resurrecting state authority. It will confine International Paper v. Ouellette's source-state savings rule to suits applying the source state's law under the Clean Water Act's saving clauses, and will reject respondents' recharacterization of the claims as ordinary deception and marketing torts, holding that the alleged injuries run through cross-border emissions. It will sustain jurisdiction under Cox Broadcasting's fourth exception rather than dismissing.

The ground will be stated as a categorical rule, not a Boulder-specific one: no state's law may supply damages remedies for injuries attributed to the effects of interstate and international greenhouse-gas emissions on the global climate, whatever the forum state and whatever the tort label (nuisance, trespass, unjust enrichment, consumer deception) where the theory of injury depends on cross-border emissions — a holding that forecloses the pending state and municipal climate-damages suits nationwide. The majority will expressly leave open claims addressing purely in-state pollution from in-state sources and garden-variety misrepresentation claims whose injury does not run through global emissions.
